label: The Latin Mass Society
blurb: Thursday evenings in the crypt chapel: the older form learned rubric by rubric from a priest who drives in from the country. The house notices who goes down those stairs, and in these years that is a compliment more than a mark.
builds: Latin, piety, the traditional wing; the older Mass, in time

credentialAfter.line: You can celebrate the older Mass now, slowly and without error. Two men in the house have asked you to teach them.

hint: They notice which way a man leans: the ones who go down those stairs have shown an interest in the older form, in the Latin, in the rubrics done well, for a year or more. Loving the older Mass is not held against the newer one, and nobody down there holds it against you.

label: The Thomists
blurb: A Dominican from the priory across town leads the Summa on Tuesday nights, one article at a time, with beer after. Nobody leaves early.
builds: theology, the intellectual pillar, an argument you can win

credentialAfter.line: You have read the Secunda Secundae through, which almost no priest of the diocese can say. The Dominican shakes your hand.

label: Disputatio
blurb: A philosophy and theology discussion circle that meets to disagree. Positions are taken, and remembered.

label: Ascetics Anonymous
blurb: Twelve steps toward holiness, taken with a straight face: a fast on Fridays, a holy hour kept together, an accountability that is half joke and wholly serious.
builds: piety, the spiritual pillar, a body used to less

label: The Admin Warriors
blurb: The men who run the house: the sacristy schedule, the class fund, the retreat logistics, the rector's spreadsheets. Unglamorous, and the chancery hears their names first.

credentialAfter.line: The rector tells the vicar for clergy that you can run a building. It goes in the file.

label: The running club
blurb: Six in the morning, four miles, in every weather, with the men who will not let you sleep in. The body keeps its accounts; this pays into them.
builds: presence, and a body that bears a long week

label: The Thursday club
blurb: Cards, the game, the argument about the professor, and a standing table at the bar down the hill. Where the class becomes a class, and where it finds out who cannot hold his drink.
builds: presence, the human pillar, a class that will remember you

label: The Hispanic ministry circle
blurb: Spanish over supper, a Mass served at the immigrant parish on Sundays, and a diocese that is watching who shows up.
builds: Spanish, the people, the pastoral pillar

credentialAfter.line: You heard your first confession in Spanish, badly, and the woman thanked you anyway. The vocation director has written it down.

label: The schola
blurb: Chant on Wednesday nights and the Sunday Mass in the seminary chapel. A voice, and an ear, and the bishop hears it at the Chrism Mass.

label: The rector's table
blurb: Dinner with the rector and his guests once a month: the auxiliary bishop, a donor, a visiting theologian. Four men are asked. The rest of the house knows which four.
builds: the chancery, the rector, connections that outlast the seminary

credentialAfter.line: The auxiliary bishop asks after you by name at the Chrism Mass. The rector does not look surprised.

hint: The rector asks the men whose evaluations read well and who have kept the house rule without being asked; the invitation comes with a good year behind it.

label: The jail Thursday
blurb: Thursday evenings at the county jail with the chaplain: a rosary in a cinder-block room, a Bible study nobody is made to attend, and men who can tell in a minute whether you are afraid of them.
builds: the pastoral pillar, presence, a name at the chancery for the hard work

credentialAfter.line: A man you have sat with for a year is released on a Tuesday and asks for your address. The chaplain tells the vocation director that you are one of the ones who keeps coming.

label: The Newman Center crew
blurb: Sunday nights at the state university's Catholic center: a Mass that starts late, pizza, and a room of twenty-year-olds who will ask you anything and can tell when you are performing.
builds: presence, the human pillar, a way with the young that the diocese is short of

credentialAfter.line: Two of the Newman students have applied to the seminary and named you on the form. The vocation director has noticed, and so, in a different tone, has the formation office.

label: The homily circle
blurb: Wednesday after supper, one man preaches for eight minutes to six others, and then they tell him the truth. It is the only room in the house where the truth about preaching is told.
builds: preaching, the pastoral pillar, a voice of your own

credentialAfter.line: You preached the eight minutes without notes and the room, which does not do this, said nothing for a while. The homiletics professor has heard about the circle and asked who is in it.

label: The Respect Life group
blurb: Thursday evenings with the diocese's pro-life people: the prayer vigil, the pregnancy center's shelves, the January bus, and the woman who has run it for twenty years and knows every pastor's phone number.
builds: the pastoral pillar, presence, a name among the diocese's most organized laypeople

contact.who: who runs the diocese's respect-life work

credentialAfter.line: Twenty Thursdays in, she has stopped introducing you as the seminarian and started introducing you as one of hers, which in that circle is a credential the chancery hears about.

label: Teaching at the parish school
blurb: Two mornings a week in a parish school: seventh-grade religion, the eighth-grade retreat, a principal who has seen thirty seminarians come and go and can tell in a week which ones the children will listen to.
builds: presence, learning, the pastoral pillar, and children who remember which priest taught them

contact.who: the principal of the parish school

credentialAfter.line: The principal writes to the vocation director, unasked, that the seventh grade would follow you into a burning building, which is not in the file's vocabulary and goes in the file anyway.

label: The nursing home Sundays
blurb: Sunday afternoons at the Catholic nursing home: the rosary in the day room, the communion round with the deacon, the residents who wait for you and the ones who no longer know they are waiting.
builds: piety, the pastoral pillar, and the patience the old require

contact.who: who runs the pastoral care at the nursing home

credentialAfter.line: The director of pastoral care tells the chaplain that the residents ask for you by name, and the chaplain, who is a retired priest of the diocese, tells the vocation director, who writes it down.

label: The soup kitchen Saturdays
blurb: Saturday mornings at the downtown kitchen: two hundred meals, the line at the door at seven, a man who has run it since the eighties on no money, and the people the city does not otherwise see.
builds: presence, the pastoral pillar, and a name among the poor and the people who serve them

contact.who: who runs the downtown soup kitchen

credentialAfter.line: The man who runs the kitchen, who does not say much, hands you the keys one Saturday and goes to his daughter's, and the line at seven is yours. He tells the pastor of the cathedral, who tells the bishop.
